title: Derive recursive NodeAuthority hashes
description: OBJECTIVE: compose canonical NodeDefinition bodies into the recursive execution-contract hashes required by design line 255. HARD DEPENDENCY: task-66250d8356e44bfc9d34d3e6f36264a0 must be DONE. DELIVERABLE: one focused @moe/scheduler module and exact LF bridge that takes a production-validated graph snapshot plus admitted NodeDefinition bodies, proves a 1:1 node set and exact direct-hard edge/contract closure, checks every DependencyContract.graphBindingDigest against the server-derived structural snapshot identity, then derives nodeAuthorityHash values iteratively in topological order from each node's canonical body, repository base/applicable policy/completion linkage, and sorted incoming edge key/type/contract plus server-derived predecessor hash. nodeKey is paired with the hash in the result rather than injected into the hash; graph/revision ids and outgoing consumers are excluded. No caller predecessor/node hash has authority. NOT IN SCOPE: GraphRevisionContent bytes/root export/daemon persistence. The GraphRevisionContent v3 task filed next is the real consumer.
definitionOfDone: Production returns a deeply frozen canonical node-authority set with exactly one entry per validated snapshot node and derives hashes iteratively in stable topological/incoming producer+edge order without recursion-depth risk or caller-provided predecessor hashes.

Every snapshot HARD edge has exactly one matching admitted direct-hard contract and no advisory edge has one; edge key/endpoints/kind, structural snapshot binding, monotonic proof, witness consistency, repository base, policy slice and completion linkage are all checked before hashing.

Malformed, missing/extra/duplicate node, missing/extra/duplicate contract, endpoint/kind/binding mismatch, cycle/graph validation, proof/witness conflict and derivation failures return exact stable code plus layer while preserving source dependency/graph code and source layer.

A nonempty >=3-node/2-hard-edge test asserts exact node/edge/hash counts, positive field/hostile rosters, descendant-only hash propagation, unchanged ancestor/unrelated hashes, revision/status exclusion, and mutation drills against the production node-field and predecessor-hash preimages.
The exact LF bridge and <=250-line production source are pinned; `pnpm --filter @moe/scheduler test` exits 0 with nonzero counts and records the GraphRevisionContent consumer task id.
taskRails: Use validateGraphSnapshot plus the existing hard-graph index/topological helpers; do not reimplement graph or DependencyContract semantics.
DependencyContract.graphBindingDigest equals the production structure-only snapshot identity, never the final graphContentHash; fail closed rather than solving a hash fixed point.

TWO PLAN CASES TURNED OUT TO BE FALSE, and I did not write them as specified.

1. "TWO GRAPHS DIFFERING ONLY IN A NODEKEY RENAME PRODUCE EQUAL HASH MULTISETS." This is NOT true and must not be asserted. A whole-graph rename changes the DependencyContract endpoint keys AND the graphBindingDigest (which is `snapshotIdentityHash`, i.e. the structural identity, which covers node keys), and both enter the preimage through the incoming section. It also changes `completionLinkage`, which equals the nodeKey on a COMPLETION node by the codec's own linkage rule. Writing the plan's version would have forced a WRONG implementation — one that dropped the contract from the preimage to make the test pass.
The honest form of the same claim, which I did write: a FAN-IN fixture where node-a and node-b each feed the completion node, neither has an incoming edge, and their bodies are identical in every projected field. Their hashes must be EQUAL — which is exactly "the key is paired, not hashed", is true, and is killed by drill (v). Pinning note: `nodeDraft`'s default objective embeds the nodeKey, so the two siblings pin an identical objective explicitly; without that the test would fail for the wrong reason.

2. TWO ROSTER CODES ARE UNREACHABLE THROUGH THE ENTRY POINT, and I disclose both rather than faking arms.
- NODE_AUTHORITY_RECURSION_CYCLE: `validateGraphSnapshot` returns ok only for an acyclic HARD subgraph, so `topologicalOrder(...).acyclic === false` cannot be observed here. The cyclic-snapshot test MEASURES that the graph layer answers, which is what step 2 told me to record.
- NODE_AUTHORITY_RECURSION_CONTRACT_DUPLICATE: unreachable by construction. Two bodies cannot file one edgeKey, because the endpoint check requires `contract.consumerNodeKey === the body's nodeKey`; and one body cannot file it twice, because the codec refuses NODE_AUTHORITY_DUPLICATE_EDGE@NODE_AUTHORITY_DEPENDENCIES first (node-authority-fields.ts:117-120). The test MEASURES that codec refusal instead of asserting my claim.
Both stay as fail-closed defences and both are named in a test that also pins the roster size at 13, so adding a code without an arm is visible.

ARMS, each pinning the LITERAL code and LITERAL layer: graph passthrough (GRAPH_ code under GRAPH_SNAPSHOT); NODE_MISSING; NODE_DUPLICATE; NODE_EXTRA; CONTRACT_MISSING; CONTRACT_FORBIDDEN (a contract filed against the ADVISORY edge); ENDPOINT_MISMATCH; BINDING_MISMATCH; WITNESS_CONFLICT (same witnessRef, two versions across two bodies); REPOSITORY_BASE_CONFLICT; COMPLETION_LINKAGE_INVALID; MALFORMED; plus TWO codec passthroughs asserting DIFFERENT source layers (NODE_AUTHORITY_MALFORMED@ADMISSION and NODE_AUTHORITY_UNSUPPORTED_SCHEMA@SCHEMA) — one pair alone could be a hard-coded constant, two prove the source layer really travels.

CONTROLS: exactly one entry per snapshot node in nodeKey order; hardEdgeCount 2; every hash 64-hex; frozen result; deterministic across two calls; three distinct hashes. PROPAGATION: an ancestor body change moves A, B and C; a descendant-only change moves C alone and leaves A and B byte-identical.

deriveNodeAuthoritySet(snapshotInput, bodiesInput, policyOverride?), staged so each layer answers for itself:
validateGraphSnapshot -> admitNodeDefinition per body -> 1:1 node set -> contract closure -> cross-body agreement -> buildHardGraphIndex + topologicalOrder -> iterate.
PLAN DEVIATION, measured in step 1: the plan's `registryInput?` parameter does not exist, because `admitNodeDefinition` takes ONE argument — a body's own persisted monotonicPredicateProofs ARE its registry (codec :143). An accepted-but-ignored parameter would have been dead surface.

THE PREIMAGE. Domain "MOE-NODE-AUTHORITY-RECURSIVE/2", separate from the body digest domain so the two rotate apart. Length-framed everywhere, so no field can shift across a boundary into its neighbour. The node section is `canonicalText` of the admitted body PROJECTED onto 15 design-255 keys; the incoming section is one frame group per arc in `hardIn` order (producer key, edge key — already deterministic, built by the graph index, not by me) carrying edgeKey, graph edge kind, satisfactionPredicate ref, the contract's canonical text, and the PREDECESSOR HASH FROM THIS MODULE'S OWN MAP.
EXCLUDED FROM THE NODE PROJECTION, each for a stated reason: `nodeKey` (paired with the hash in the result — design 255 does not list it), `schemaVersion` (rides the domain tag), `directHardDependencies` and `monotonicPredicateProofs` (they enter through the incoming section instead, where the order is graph-derived rather than body-declared; including them twice would let a body's own edge ordering influence an identity the graph is supposed to fix).

WHAT THIS MODULE ACTUALLY DECIDES — only what no single body can see: that the body set and the graph are one node set (missing / extra / duplicate, three distinct codes); that every HARD edge has exactly one contract, filed on its CONSUMER's body, with endpoints matching the snapshot edge; that every contract's graphBindingDigest equals `snapshotIdentityHash(graph)` — task rail 2's structural identity, never a graphContentHash; that no ADVISORY or unknown edge carries a contract; that one witnessRef never carries two different digest/version seals across bodies; that all bodies share one repositoryBaseTree; and that the graph's completion node is exactly the node claiming joinRole COMPLETION.
That last rule is MINE, not a mirror: I checked `applicable()` and it decides node/criterion/recipe applicability only — it has no completion invariant to mirror, because it never sees a graph. The codec's own linkage rule (fields.ts:210-211) is body-local: role NONE means linkage null, COMPLETION means linkage equals the nodeKey, JOIN means non-null. Neither can see which node the GRAPH calls completion, so that is the gap this check fills.

NO CALLER HASH IS READ ANYWHERE. Predecessor hashes come from the local map keyed by producer nodeKey; the codec already refuses a body that so much as states nodeAuthorityHash or predecessorAuthorityHash (NODE_AUTHORITY_FORBIDDEN_IDENTITY_KEYS). Derivation is a single `for` over Kahn's order — no recursion, so a deep chain costs a loop step rather than a stack frame (DoD 1).

25 DRILLS, one at a time, SHA-256-verified byte-exact restores (git diff is blind to my three untracked files, so sha256 is the instrument). 23 RED by NAME. Two survivors: ONE was a real hole in my tests that I closed, and ONE is a disclosed equivalent mutant with the reason PROVEN by a test rather than argued.

THE ONE THAT MATTERED — DoD 4's named drill, and it SURVIVED on the first pass. G1 dropped `capability` from the node projection and the whole suite stayed green: 26 passed, zero failures. My tests varied only `objective`, so the design-255 field roster was NARRATED, not asserted — exactly the defect the drill exists to find. I then drilled ALL FIFTEEN projected fields one at a time; 13 of 15 survived at that point.
FIX: a per-field sweep, one case per field, each moving exactly that field and asserting node-a's hash moves. Needed three new fixture knobs (a generic draft `patch`, a `planPatch` and an `acceptancePatch`) so the derived fields could move through their PLANNING records rather than by hand, and the plan fixture gained "recipe-b" so `verificationRecipeRevisions` could vary while staying applicable. `repositoryBaseTree` moves on all three bodies because the module requires them to agree.
RE-DRILLED all 15: 13 now red on their own named case ("moves node-a's hash when <field> moves").

THE SECOND SURVIVOR, and the honest handling. `completionLinkage` and `joinRole` both still survived, because my single case moved BOTH at once — a two-fields-one-case mask. I split it:
- `completionLinkage` now has a dedicated pair (both bodies JOIN, only the linkage differs: "node-b" vs "node-c"). Re-drilled: RED on "moves the hash when only completionLinkage moves".
- `joinRole` CANNOT be isolated, and that is a property of the admission rules, not a gap. The codec determines the legal linkage FROM the role (NONE demands null, JOIN demands non-null, COMPLETION demands the nodeKey — fields.ts:210-211) and this module requires the COMPLETION role to sit on the graph's completion node. No two admissible bodies for one node differ in the role alone. Dropping `joinRole` from the projection is therefore an EQUIVALENT MUTANT. It stays in because design 255 names join/completion linkage, and the linkage half carries the assertion. I pinned the coupling with a test that MEASURES both halves: (JOIN, null) throws NODE_AUTHORITY_JOIN_LINKAGE_INVALID@NODE_AUTHORITY_ADMISSION at the codec, and (COMPLETION, "node-a") on a non-completion node refuses NODE_AUTHORITY_RECURSION_COMPLETION_LINKAGE_INVALID here.

THE PLAN'S FIVE, all RED, each reddening EXACTLY ONE named test:
(i) node-field preimage -> see G1 above, now red on every field.
(ii) predecessor hash frame replaced by a constant -> "changes a node and every descendant when an ancestor body changes". Recursion is load-bearing.
(iii) graphBindingDigest comparison short-circuited -> "refuses a graphBindingDigest that is not the structural snapshot identity". The check is live, not answered by an earlier layer.
(iv) advisory-edge refusal removed -> "refuses a contract filed against an ADVISORY edge".
(v) nodeKey injected into the projection -> "gives two sibling nodes that differ ONLY in nodeKey the identical hash". The paired-not-hashed claim.
